An elbow-length-sleeved crew-neck cotton T-shirt, a real plain T-shirt and not a real garment, covered edge to edge in a lightly distressed worn-in print, designed to make the shirt look like the outfit of a teacher. The outfit's colours flood the entire front and both sleeves as one continuous print, and the back carries the matching back of the outfit. The outfit is printed across the whole front, over the shoulders and down both sleeves, showing a tweed jacket with chalk-dusted elbow patches. The print wraps all the way round, the back of the shirt shows the rear of the outfit from the back collar to the hem and along both sleeves. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. The shirt is an ordinary T-shirt ending in a straight bottom hem, and the garment printed on it runs straight down the whole shirt to that hem. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt's sleeves are tailored to end at the elbow, exactly where the outfit's sleeves end. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It also shows printed cuffs at the sleeve hems. The print wraps around the sides so the outfit seems to continue around the body. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit and the most recognisable props and accessories of the outfit as appliqué pieces, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed deep brown skin tone.

The outfit's front panels run straight down the shirt's front with its shoulders sitting on the shirt's shoulder seams, and its sleeves are printed along the shirt's sleeves to cuffs at the sleeve hems, showing a worn old suit under a cardigan. Turn the shirt around and the back carries the matching back of the outfit, printed edge to edge with nothing left plain. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is stretched to the shirt's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. A long-sleeved shirt is used so the outfit's long sleeves fit exactly, printed full length to the shirt's wrist hems. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It also shows printed cuffs where the sleeves end. The illusion is purely flat and two-dimensional, with no real fabric, buttons or pockets beyond the print. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, the outfit's patches, insignia and emblems and the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed deep brown skin tone.
A long-sleeved crew-neck cotton T-shirt, a real plain T-shirt and not a real garment, covered edge to edge in a hyper-realistic sublimation print showing the real outfit in fine detail, designed to make the shirt look like the outfit of a train conductor. The printed outfit runs from the neckline to the hem and from one sleeve hem to the other, its shoulders on the shirt's shoulder seams, showing a double-breasted jacket with brass buttons and a watch chain. The print wraps all the way round, the back of the shirt shows the rear of the outfit from the back collar to the hem and along both sleeves. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. Everything is flat ink on opaque cotton, lace, tulle, fur, feathers, sequins, armour and metal appear as printed patterns. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It also shows a printed collar continuing the outfit up to the neckline and printed gloves emerging at the sleeve hems. The print wraps around the sides so the outfit seems to continue around the body. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve, the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit and its pockets, flaps and trims, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed deep brown skin tone.
